newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse confident after good Q1.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse confident after good Q1.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group, Switzerland's second biggest bank group, said on Monday it was confident of meeting mid-term financial goals after getting off to a very good start in the first quarter of 1997.
CS Group said the first three months of the year saw revenues from balance sheet business, commissions and trading activities significantly higher than the year-ago period.
Expenses and provisions developed in line with management expectations, the group said in a statement.
"Credit Suisse Group has started 1997 with a very good first quarter," it added.
"All four business units achieved strong earnings improvements compared with the average quarterly operating results for 1996," it added without elabortainmg.

The four areas created in a major restructuring at the start of this year are domestic retail and corporate bank Credit Suisse, international corporate and invesment bank Credit Suisse First Boston, CS Private Banking and CS Asset Managment.
The group is second biggest in Switzerland to Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).
CS Group said its new corporate structure, launched on January 1 to streamline operations by business areas and cut duplication, was proving successful.

"Given the progress to date in the restructuring and the very good start to the year, Credit Suisse Group is confident that it will make significant steps toward achieving its medium-term financial targets in the course of 1997," it said.
Chief executive Lukas Muehlemann said in March the group's return on equity goal was 15 percent.
In 1996 the return on equity, in respect with the operating result, was 10.1 percent and 9.6 percent after minority interests.
Credit Suisse's group operating profit after minorities in 1996 eased to 1.638 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion) from 1.695 million.

But due to extraordinary charges for restructuring and for providing for bad loans, the CS Group plunged into a 1996 net loss of 2.59 billion francs after minorities compared with a net profit of 1.401 billion in 1995.
As in the past, CS Group did not provide figures for its first quarter performance.
"The restructuring of Credit Suisse, whichs serves domestic individual and corporate clients, is progressing according to plan," the statement said.
Revenues remained at "average quarterly levels for 1996" but expenses were lower.
CS Private Banking and Asset Management benefitted from good financial markets and an increase in the volume of assets under management, the group said.

"Credit Suisse First Boston...posted significantly higher revenues and results, due mainly to the good conditions in the securities markets in the first two months of the year," it said. ($ = 1.468 Swiss Francs)
